I found 13 methods that call `trace::async_op` directly, all in the `tokio` crate. Every call uses the qualified path `trace::async_op(`. I found no imports or aliases of it under another name. The only hits in other crates or in tests are span-name strings, not calls.

- **`tokio/src/sync/mutex.rs`:** `Mutex::lock` and `Mutex::lock_owned`
- **`tokio/src/sync/rwlock.rs`:** `RwLock::read`, `RwLock::read_owned`, `RwLock::write` and `RwLock::write_owned`
- **`tokio/src/sync/semaphore.rs`:** `Semaphore::acquire`, `Semaphore::acquire_many`, `Semaphore::acquire_owned` and `Semaphore::acquire_many_owned`
- **`tokio/src/sync/barrier.rs`:** `Barrier::wait`
- **`tokio/src/sync/oneshot.rs`:** `Sender::closed`
- **`tokio/src/time/interval.rs`:** `Interval::tick`

Some files, such as `time/sleep.rs`, `sync/oneshot.rs` and `sync/batch_semaphore.rs`, create spans named `runtime.resource.async_op` by hand with `tracing::trace_span!`. Those don't call the function, so I left them out.
